data.title: Flooding in Bangkok and 20 provinces
data.description: Flooding persisted in parts of Bangkok and in 20 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were declining, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Monday.

data.title: Traffickers caught with red panda in Mae Sot
data.description: Two men were arrested after police found a protected red panda in their vehicle during a road stop near the Myanmar border in Tak province and they could not produce a permit legalising possesssion.

data.title: Rain, runoff, rocks and mud slam Phuket
data.description: PHUKET - Persistent rain caused runoff that washed big rocks and mud into communities and tourist venues in this southern island province early Monday morning.

data.title: Public 'not convinced' by welfare policies
data.description: Some 64.85% of respondents lack confidence in the Anutin Charnvirakul government's welfare provision, with others saying Thais have limited access to state benefits, a Suan Dusit Poll survey has found.

data.title: Democrats prepare lawsuit over Bangkok flood claims
data.description: The Democrat Party is preparing to sue the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration and other state agencies in the Administrative Court over alleged negligence in handling floods in the capital, seeking full compensation for affected residents.

data.title: Pressure mounts over sea ruling
data.description: Thailand should endorse the 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award to protect its maritime trade interests, preserve regional peace and uphold the maritime framework Unclos, says former Philippine Supreme Court Justice Antonio Carpio.

data.title: Ex-Democrat MP slams online gambling crackdown
data.description: Former Democrat Party MP Sirichok Sopha has questioned the effectiveness of the Digital Economy and Society (DES) Ministry's crackdown on online gambling, claiming major websites remain accessible despite the blocking of nearly one million URLs.

data.title: Govt insists border  artefacts are Thai
data.description: Culture Minister Sabeeda Thaised has rejected Cambodia's demand for the return of artefacts found at Prasat Khana on the Thai-Cambodian border, insisting the items are Thai antiquities protected under Thai law.

data.title: Opposition to discuss censure plan
data.description: Opposition parties are scheduled to meet on Wednesday to discuss the timetable for a no-confidence debate, with the Democrat Party insisting it needs at least four days to grill the government.

data.title: Province hailed for green rice farming
data.description: SUPHAN BURI: Suphan Buri province has been praised as a flagship pilot for low-carbon rice cultivation, as research reveals Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) water management can reduce greenhouse gas emissions by half.

data.title: Engineer held over burglary
data.description: A 28-year-old electrical engineer has been arrested in Nonthaburi for allegedly stealing valuables worth more than 2 million baht from a house after losing over 200,000 baht trading gold.

data.title: Floods spur debate over city pond plan
data.description: Severe flooding in Bangkok in late September has reignited a dispute over the proposed Bueng Khu Bon retention pond, raising questions about whether the capital should build more large-scale water-retention facilities or prioritise improvements to existing drainage systems.

data.title: Govt plans Prachin Buri River probe
data.description: A thorough investigation is needed to determine what caused aquatic animals to die in the Prachin Buri River, deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana said.

data.title: CAAT clarifies rules on opening bags
data.description: Airport staff may open checked baggage without the passenger present only when X-ray screening raises suspicions about prohibited or dangerous items, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) said on Sunday.

data.title: Govt watching Europe unrest
data.description: The Commerce Ministry is closely monitoring protests and unrest across Europe to assess potential risks to Thai trade and exports, Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun said on Sunday.

data.title: CP distances itself, chairman from holy basil patents
data.description: Charoen Pokphand Group (CP), the country’s largest agribusiness conglomerate, has distanced itself and its senior chairman Dhanin Chearavanont from the controversial patents registered for new varieties of holy basil, a popular herb in Thai cuisine.

data.title: Black, spotted leopards filmed together in Kaeng Krachan
data.description: A wildlife photographer has reported seeing two black and three spotted leopards together on a road in Kaeng Krachan National Park, highlighting the ecological richness of the Unesco World Heritage forest.

data.title: Black, spotted leopards filmed togrther in Kaeng Krachan
data.description: A wildlife photographer has reported seeing two black and three spotted leopards together on a road in Kaeng Krachan National Park, highlighting the ecological richness of the Unesco World Heritage forest.

data.title: Traffic police ordered to unmask, start with warnings, not take bribes
data.description: Traffic police nationwide have been ordered to always show their face when disciplining motorists, to start with warnings before progressive fines, and not to take proffered bribes.

data.title: Domestic flyers also subject to new luggage search rule
data.description: Travellers on all domestic flights are also liable to have their luggage searched under new regulations, not just flyers leaving the kingdom, the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) warned on Sunday.

data.title: Flooding persists in Bangkok, 17 provinces, toll at 83
data.description: Flooding persisted in parts of Bangkok and in 17 provinces, mostly in the Central Plains, but water levels were declining, the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation reported on Sunday.

data.title: B40/day fare on Red, Purple lines likely to be extended
data.description: The Transport Ministry will propose the extension of the 40-baht day-tripper rate on the two Red Lines and the Purple line for another year, with the current promotion due to end on Nov 30.

data.title: Heavy rain in Northeast, North, Central Plains, East, South early this week
data.description: The Meteorological Department forecast is for fluctuating weather and possible heavy rain in the Northeast, North, Central Plains and East into Tuesday, and persistent rain in the South into Wednesday.

data.title: Missing Dutch celebrity left Thailand late last year - police
data.description: Missing Dutch television personality and politician Emile Ratelband, whose family is seeking information as to his whereabouts, left Thailand late last year, according to immigration police.

data.title: 'No ID, No Ads' looms
data.description: The government is intensifying its crackdown on online scams with a new "No ID, No Ads" policy taking effect on Nov 1.

data.title: Airports told to brace for rain
data.description: The Department of Airports has been instructed to prepare its facilities in the South for heavy rain, deputy government spokeswoman Ploythalay Laksameesaengjan says.

data.title: PM reaffirms commitment to global peace on UN Day
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has reaffirmed Thailand's commitment to international law, peaceful dispute resolution and global cooperation in a speech marking United Nations Day.

data.title: Navy insists on fair probe into conscript's death
data.description: The Royal Thai Navy has pledged not to shield anyone found to have committed wrongdoing in connection with the death of a conscript during training in 2024, following findings by the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) that he was assaulted and denied timely medical treatment.

data.title: Chanthaburi border fence phase one done
data.description: The first phase of the security fence at the Thai-Cambodian border is finished, while the next phases are progressing, according to local security units.

data.title: Social media guidelines given to NACC staff
data.description: The National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) has issued new guidelines restricting officials' use of social media during working hours and prohibiting online conduct that could undermine the agency's reputation and public confidence.

data.title: Governors to collect royal fireboxes on Nov 20
data.description: Interior permanent secretary Unsit Sampuntharat has ordered provincial governors to collect royal fireboxes at Government House on Nov 20 for public sandalwood-flower offerings honouring the late Queen Mother.

data.title: Agriculture dept to review holy basil registration bid
data.description: Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Suriya Juangroongruangkit has ordered an investigation into a company's application for plant variety protection covering four holy basil varieties, amid concerns the move could affect farmers' rights and traditional cultivation practices.

data.title: GDP will beat 2.1%  forecast, PM says
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the Office of the National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC) to reassess its GDP outlook after key economic indicators improved.
